Two changes that CANNOT alter behaviour, kept because 'we tried this and it survived, and here is why' is worth more than silence.  Both rest on one property of bitreverse (src/pump/v34/v34rx.c): with nbits == 7 it returns a value in 0..127, so it is non-negative and fits in three bits after a shift of four.  Nothing else is held fixed -- neither depends on any input this test chooses.
the three-bit slice of the reversed Uinfo is masked to four bits
why: bitreverse(v, 7) is at most 127, so (r >> 4) is at most 7 and the two masks select the same bits.  The arithmetic shift is kept in the source because it is what the object does, not because it can change an answer.

label: the reversed field is shifted logically rather than arithmetically
why: the only input is bitreverse(_, 7), which is non-negative, so the sign of the shifted value never differs.  The object uses cwtl and sar; that is transcribed rather than simplified so it stays true if the field ever widens.

label: Two more that survive, and for the same kind of reason: a bit the mask clears is put straight back by the constant OR-ed in after it, and a bit the gather sets is above the three bitreverse(_, 3) reads.  Neither is a gap in the test -- no input can distinguish them -- and both are transcribed as the object has them rather than simplified.
the answer arm clears three bits of index 3, not two
why: the extra bit the wider mask clears is bit 3, and both of the two constants OR-ed in afterwards (9 and 0xb) set bit 3.  So the object's own mask has a redundant bit in it; ~6 is transcribed because that is the instruction, not because it is the minimum.

label: the recovered baud index takes three bits of index 2
why: the third bit lands at position 3 of the gathered value and bitreverse(v, 3) reads only positions 0, 1 and 2 (src/pump/v34/v34rx.c).  Nothing this test chooses can make it observable, and the same is true of any input at all.
